> A shared-mode fix so `apps update` works again on an app repo left owned by another uid.

### Upgrade Steps

* [ACTION REQUIRED] Anyone running shared mode should update to v3.1.2. After updating, run `cwcli restart <instance>` once per instance so the self-heal re-owns the instance's app source repositories - or, to repair a single app in place without a full restart, run `cwcli apps update <instance> <app> --force`.

### Bug Fixes

* **`apps update --force` now clears git's "dubious ownership" refusal on an app repo owned by another uid.** On a shared-mode or migrated instance, an app's source is often symlinked out of the bench to a shared tree (for example `/workspace/.hdsrc/<app>`) and stays owned by the pre-shared uid, so both `git pull` and the `git status` the conflict path relies on used to fail - making `--force` powerless. It now re-owns the real repo behind the symlink to the `frappe` user before pulling.
* **Shared-mode self-heal on `cwcli start`/`restart` now also re-owns app source repositories that live outside the bench.** v3.1.1 re-owned the bench workspace itself but never followed `apps/<app>` symlinks out of it, so a migrated instance's app repos stayed stranded at the pre-shared uid and a plain `apps update` kept failing even after a restart. A restart now re-owns those repos too, so `apps update` works without needing `--force`.
